description: Get the user a free HLA-Verify API key, instantly. HLA-Verify is free for anyone: the key comes back in this result (status issued, field key) with 1,000 calls/day, 250 typings per call and 60 requests/minute; the user sends it as the X-API-Key header (or connects this MCP server with it). Ask before calling: it stores the email address with the key, used for service notices only. The key is shown once: give it to the user straight away. One key per address; asking again returns already_issued and never the key (lost keys: hello@hlaverify.com). Disposable inboxes are refused. Verified labs that need more can set tier "lab" with institution and use_case to apply for the Lab tier (10,000 calls/day, 5,000 typings per call): that is reviewed, and an approved key is emailed.

email.description: The user's email address. Stored with the key; service notices only.

expected_volume.description: Rough call or typing volume, e.g. 'about 20,000 typings a month' (optional).

institution.description: Lab, hospital, university, registry or company (optional; required with tier lab).

source.description: Where the request came from, e.g. mcp (optional).

tier.description: Omit for a free key now. "lab" applies for the Lab tier instead (institution and use_case required).

use_case.description: What the API would be used for (optional; required with tier lab, where the decision is made on it). No patient details.

name: research_access

key.description: The API key, only when status is issued. Give it to the user; it is not shown again.

ok.description: Always true; a refused request comes back as an error result.

release.description: IPD-IMGT/HLA release every verdict was computed against.

status.description: issued: `key` holds a new free key, shown only this once. already_issued: this address already has a key (never shown again; lost keys: hello@hlaverify.com). recorded/already_recorded: a Lab-tier application (tier "lab") is on file. All are success; do not retry.
